subject: Horizon Analytics - throughput collapse -> cross-region failover & latency spikes
messages:
From: Devon Price <devon@horizon.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: US-WEST-2 throughput collapse — production traffic failing

Jordan,

We started seeing a massive throughput collapse in us-west-2 at ~08:50 PDT. Requests are queuing for >10s and we’re seeing a 25% 5xx rate on our customer-facing endpoints that hit Redwood. This is impacting our onboarding flows and billing ingestion.

We rolled back a config change but the error rate persisted. Our SRE applied rate-limiting on the client side to reduce retries which helped, but we cannot sustain degraded SLA. Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing any regional capacity issues or routing changes? We need an estimated time to recovery and a mitigation plan — Horizon will need exec-level updates in 30 minutes.

Attaching a short log sample.

—Devon
Devon Price
Head of Platform, Horizon Analytics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Price <devon@horizon.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:18:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: US-WEST-2 throughput collapse — production traffic failing

Devon — thanks for the heads up and logs. We’re on it.

Immediate actions:
- I’ve opened a P0 bridge (link below) and routed SRE + on-call infra.
- Can you confirm whether Horizon pinned to a specific AZ within us-west-2 or if traffic is region-wide? That will change the mitigation.
- We will start a controlled cross-region drain to us-east-1 as a temporary failover if capacity in us-west-2 cannot be restored within 20 minutes.

I’ve looped Hannah (runtime lead) and Marissa (customer success) for coordination and exec comms. We’ll update you in the bridge in 10.

Bridge: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/horizon-20290514
—Jordan
VP, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:20:55 -07:00
Subject: ACTION: Horizon production — us-west-2 throughput collapse 

Team — Devon just reported a region-wide throughput collapse for Horizon in us-west-2. Key facts from customer logs attached.

Ask list (first 30m):
1) Hannah: can you validate whether the serving fleet in us-west-2 is healthy (node counts, queue depth, GPU memory pressure)? If we have a degraded pool, can we spin up extra compatible capacity in us-west-2 first?
2) Vivek: double-check routing rules for Horizon’s tenant (customer pinning / preferred-region). If they are pinned to us-west-2, prepare the config to allow immediate region failover to us-east-1.
3) Marissa: prep an exec note for Horizon leadership and Redwood commercial (prepare one with options for 1) temporary cross-region failover, 2) SLAs/credits if hit, 3) longer-term suggested regional capacity).

If we can’t get stable in 20 minutes, I want a pre-approved plan to fail traffic to us-east-1 with a selectable routing window. I’m attaching a quick MPAN with temporary route entries — feel free to edit and backfill.

Attachments: temporary-routing-mpan.xlsx, horizon-error-sample-logs.txt

—Jordan

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:32:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: Horizon production — us-west-2 throughput collapse 

Jordan / team — initial findings from infra:
- us-west-2 serving pool shows elevated KV cache evictions followed by continuous batching backlog. Node CPU/GPU looks OK, but KV cache pressure is causing per-request path fallbacks that amplify latency.
- There is a transient networking flake between two AZs (az2 <-> az3) that appears to have caused asymmetric load which pushed certain shards into hot loops.

Immediate mitigations applied (completed):
- Disabled aggressive prefetching for impacted model shard groups (drops QPS by ~12% but reduces queueing).
- Scaled one compatible dedicated pool in us-west-2 by +20% (hot spare).

If latency and 5xx rate don’t fall to acceptable SLA in next 10–15 minutes, we recommend controlled cross-region failover to us-east-1 for Horizon’s production traffic. I’ve posted SRE bridge notes here: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/horizon-20290514 (section: infra-actions).

I’ll monitor KV cache metrics and queue depth closely and update every 10 minutes.

—Hannah
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Price <devon@horizon.ai>, Ethan Zhang <ethan@horizon.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:50:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: US-WEST-2 throughput collapse — production traffic failing

Devon / Ethan — short customer-facing update: 

What we saw: asymmetric AZ networking flake in us-west-2 caused KV cache pressure and batching backlogs that increased tail latency and 5xxs for requests routed to impacted shards.
What we did: disabled aggressive prefetching, scaled hot spare capacity in us-west-2, and prepared a failover to us-east-1.
What’s next (recommended): controlled region failover to us-east-1 for Horizon’s production route. This will restore throughput and reduce queueing immediately but trade off an extra ~80–120ms regional RTT for some requests and potential cold-cache quality variance for a small subset of model responses.

If you approve, we’ll execute a staged reroute (5% -> 25% -> 100%) over 15 minutes with SRE monitoring and automatic rollback on error. We will keep logs and an mpan of actions and can open a special postmortem with redwood infra.

Also attaching interim bridge notes and logs for your security/compliance team.

—Jordan
VP, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachments: sre-bridge-notes.pdf

From: Ethan Zhang <ethan@horizon.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Devon Price <devon@horizon.ai>
Cc: Horizon SRE <sre@horizon.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 02:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: US-WEST-2 throughput collapse — production traffic failing

Jordan — appreciate the quick response and the bridge. We approved the staged failover at 10:05 PDT and saw throughput return within the first stage; 5xxs dropped to <1% and tail latencies normalized within 8 minutes of the 25% shift.

Two asks as we stabilize:
1) Can Redwood validate and share the exact model-variant mapping that was used in us-east-1 during the failover? We had a 0.7% delta in generation quality on a small eval set and need the mapping for our audit.
2) We’ll want a postmortem and a remediation plan addressing AZ networking asymmetry and guardrails to avoid cache amplification. Horizon’s legal team may request temporary credit depending on final impact assessment — Marissa, I’ll coordinate with you on timelines.

Thanks — will stay on the bridge for follow-ups.

—Ethan
SRE, Horizon Analytics
